Remark
[Hyperbolic length minimization]

Source: petersen:page-0054, petersen:page-0055 ↗ ex:pet-ch1-hyperbolic-space ↗ rem:pet-ch1-ex-16 ↗ prop:pet-ch1-no-flat-immersion

1. ch1:1.6.21Fix $p,q\in H^n\subset \mathbb {R}^{n,1}$ and a unit $v\in T_pH^n$, so $g(p,p)=g(q,q)=-1$, $g(v,v)=1$, and $g(p,v)=0$. Then:

  1. $p\cosh t+v\sinh t$ is unit speed with initial data $(p,v)$;

  2. $F(r,v)=p\cosh r+v\sinh r$ is a diffeomorphism $(0,\infty )\times S^{n-1}\to H^n\setminus \{ p\} $;

  3. if $q=F(r_0,v_0)$, then

    \[ \partial _r|_q =\frac{-p-(q\cdot p)q}{\sqrt{-1+(q\cdot p)^2}} =p\sinh r_0+v_0\cosh r_0; \]

  4. every curve from $p$ to $q$ has length at least $r_0$, with equality only along the corresponding hyperbola;

  5. no open $U\subset \mathbb {R}^n$ admits a Riemannian immersion into $H^n$; the source uses equilateral hyperbolic triangles, whose angles are less than $\pi /3$.

The formalization obtains the final assertion from item 3 with $\beta $ equal to the Minkowski form and $c=-1$.
